for: The Sommelier's Codex: Brennan's, 417 Royal Street, New Orleans; for a server starting Monday 5 October 2026.
method: Built from catalogue.json in this folder (153 wines, 34 dishes), the shipped pack (62 dishes, 20 wines) and the guide of 26 September 2026 (section 2, the pairing formula, and the per-dish pairing blocks). No new searches were run. Every bottle named is one the catalogue or the pack holds; every price is copied character for character from the catalogue record it cites (price_printed, price_what, price_status), never rounded. A wine whose price or vintage rests on a single source carries the flag "confirm on the list". The by-the-glass first pick is the one the pack and guide name, kept; where they name none, the card says the pick is a Codex suggestion. Bottle tiers are value, classic and splurge by price, where the list allows. Reasons, lines and serving notes are sommelier advice, not house claims. No allergen content.

principles.acid: The wine should be at least as tart as the dish: lemon, tomato, vinaigrette and mignonette need a high-acid wine.
principles.fat: Butter, cream, hollandaise and fried food want acidity or bubbles to cut through and refresh.
principles.weight: Light dishes with light wines, rich dishes with fuller wines.
principles.sweet: The wine must be at least as sweet as the dish, or it tastes thin and sour.
principles.heat: Spice wants low alcohol, low tannin and a touch of sweetness; high alcohol makes heat burn.
principles.tannin: Tannic reds love protein and fat; keep them away from oily fish and heavy spice.
principles.salt: Salt loves acid, bubbles and sweetness; umami softens with fruit and clashes with big tannin.
principles.bridge: A shared flavour (herbs, citrus, smoke, mushroom, butter, toast) ties dish and wine together.
principles.method: Grilled and smoked dishes take more body than poached ones; French-Creole food often loves French wine.
principles.source: The guide of 26 September, section 2, as the house formula; restated here so the Codex reads alone.
